explanation: Old and Middle English wrote th with the letter thorn, þ. Early printers lacked it and used a similar-looking y, so þe, the, became ye on the page.

claims.text: In 'Ye Olde', 'Ye' comes from an old written form of 'the', in which y stood in for the letter thorn (þ).
Old and Middle English used the letter thorn (þ) for the th sound.
Early printers, whose type lacked thorn, used y in its place, because the letters looked alike in late medieval handwriting.
